Hi Elena — thanks for the details and the export. Congrats on the rollout plans — happy to help get this over the line.

Quick summary proposal (high level):
- Uplift: add 10 x A40-equivalent GPUs to your reserved pool (net +10, new pool = 14 GPUs).
- Expected baseline throughput: ~48k tokens/sec sustained across the pool (measured as 60-second rolling average).
- Burst window: up to 72k tokens/sec (short bursts up to 30s, subject to autoscaling and global capacity).
- Availability & SLO: 99.5% of 1-minute throughput samples meeting the baseline over a 30-day SLA window.
- Credits: service credits prorated by the % shortfall for sustained degradations beyond the error budget; details in attached SLO draft.

What I need from you to finalize pricing and order form: preferred start date, target go-live region (you noted us-west), and whether Sentinel wants monthly or quarterly billing. Vivek is ccʼd to drop numbers. Iʼll loop in legal for SLO language (Hannah). Marissa from CS will run the migration/kickoff plan once signed.

Proposed timeline: final sign by 2026-09-24 -> provisioning begins 2026-10-01 -> validation window 2 weeks -> Q4 go-live.

Subject: Draft SLO language and minimal changes weʼd request

Hi all — I pulled together a focused SLO annex for the reserved pool uplift Chloe proposed. Main points changed from the draft:

1) Measurement window and metric definition:
   - Baseline throughput defined as 60-second rolling average across the reserved pool, aggregated at the pool level.
   - SLO: 99.5% of 1-minute samples meet or exceed baseline in any 30-day calendar window.

2) Error budget and crediting:
   - Error budget = 0.5% of 1-minute samples per 30-day window.
   - If measured compliance falls below the SLO for >3 consecutive calendar days, customer is eligible for service credits: 5% of monthly reserved fee for the first week of failure, then 10% thereafter until remediation.

3) Maintenance & force majeure:
   - Planned maintenance windows (max 8 hours/month) excluded from SLO calculations with 72-hour notice.

4) Measurement & dispute process:
   - Redwood will publish per-pool telemetry (tokens/sec by minute) to a read-only S3 location for customer review; discrepancies flagged within 14 days are eligible for dispute.

5) Fallbacks and mitigations:
   - If pool capacity cannot meet baseline due to regional capacity constraints, automatic fallback to compatible variant model (no less than 80% of baseline performance) will be attempted; customer will be notified and credits applied only if fallback fails to meet 80% baseline for >24 hours.

Please review the attached SLO pdf. If acceptable, weʼll prepare an SLO annex and a single order form for signature (DocuSign link below). Minor redlines welcome but material changes may require additional approval cycles.
